newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere radios over audience cap-Council.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere radios over audience cap-Council.

text.p: French broadcasting regulator Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA) has told Lagardere SCA that its radio stations are over the legal limit for potential audience since Lagardere merged two subsidiaries, a Lagardere spokesman said on Thursday.

A CSA spokeswoman said the watchdog held a meeting on the subject with Lagardere officials following the announcement in April of the merger, which involved Lagardere grouping Skyrock and the smaller Chante France radio stations under the same company as its Europe 1, Europe 2 and RFM stations.
Earlier this week daily newspaper La Tribune said Lagardere may have to sell one of its radio stations because they now top the legal limit on potential audience.
Lagardere contests the CSA's calculation of its audience and rules out selling Europe 1, the Lagardere spokesman said.

The previous centre-right government instituted in 1994 a limit of 150 million potential listeners for any single radio operator under a law to prevent the concentration of the country's radios in too few hands.
"(Lagardere's radio stations) are slightly above this level. They have to find a solution," the CSA spokeswoman said.
"Europe 1 is not for sale. For the rest we will see what should be done to conform to the wishes of the CSA after the summer holidays," the Lagardere spokesman said.

He declined to say what figure Lagardere puts on the potential audience covered by its radio stations, and said the numbers were not the only important point in the talks with the CSA. He declined to elaborate.
Lagardere would still have a problem if its radio stations were just under the limit, if it sought to develop by bidding for extra FM frequencies, the CSA spokeswoman said.
In that case it would have to sell a sizeable station to be able to take on the potential audience of those frequencies without breaking through the legal limit, she said.
FM frequencies are like gold dust in France, with few national radio stations having national coverage on the FM band.

Lagardere said on April 3 it was merging Hachette Filipacchi Presse, which groups Europe 1 Communication, a 45.11 percent-owned unit of Lagardere, with Filipacchi Medias, itself the 85-percent owner of music station Skyrock, to create Hachette Filipacchi Medias.
Europe 1 Communication groups Europe 1, one of France's major privately-owned general radio stations, music stations Europe 2 and RFM and advertising space seller Europe 1 Regies.

Following the merger, which was approved on June 18, Lagardere owns 67.41 percent of Hachette Filipacchi Medias' capital and 66 percent of its voting rights, with 65.88 percent of its shares and 63 percent of its voting rights being held via Lagardere media unit Hachette SA.
